You are invited to participate in a research study about how blood pressure is measured in general practice. This study is being conducted by Prof James Sharman and the research team at the Menzies Institute for Medical Research, University of Tasmania. Please read this information carefully before deciding whether to participate. Taking part is voluntary.

Section Header: 2. What is the purpose of this study?
Field Label: This study aims to improve the accuracy of blood pressure measurement in general practice by using a method called Automated Office Blood Pressure (AOBP). AOBP is endorsed as the recommended way to measure blood pressure in Australia by Hypertension Australia and the National Hypertension Taskforce. Using this accurate method is expected to help general practitioners make more informed decisions about your care related to blood pressure.

Section Header: 3. Why have I been invited to participate?
Field Label: You are invited because you are attending a general practice that is participating in this study, and your blood pressure may be measured as part of your usual care.

Section Header: 4. What does participation involve?
Field Label: If you agree to take part, your blood pressure will be measured using an automated device while you sit quietly. This involves a short rest period followed by several automatic readings. The process takes approximately 8 minutes and is conducted by trained practice staff. In some circumstances, your blood pressure may also be measured while you are standing, and this will take a few additional minutes with a staff member present. After your blood pressure measurement, the results are recorded and retained in your medical record and may be used by your general practitioner as part of your usual medical care. You will also have the option to provide feedback to the research team about your experience having your blood pressure measured as part of the study.

Section Header: 5. What information is used for the study?
Field Label:
With your consent, the research team will collect and use information provided by you, your general practice medical record, and other routinely collected health data. This includes:

  • demographic information (name, date of birth, sex, postcode, email and phone number)
  • your AOBP measurements
  • information from your medical record relating to blood pressure and cardiovascular health
  • health data such as hospital discharge summaries and registry health information (e.g. Tasmanian Death Registry) linked via the Tasmanian Data Linkage Unit

This information is used to understand issues relating to blood pressure measurement and management over time, and to assess health outcomes related to blood pressure.

Section Header: 6. Are there any possible benefits from participation in this study?
Field Label: You may benefit from a more accurate blood pressure measurement to help guide your care. The findings from this study may also help improve blood pressure care for other patients in the future.

Section Header: 7. Are there any possible risks from participation in this study?
Field Label: The risks are the same as routine blood pressure measurement. You may feel brief discomfort while the cuff tightens around your arm, or concern if a high blood pressure reading is identified.

Section Header: 8. How will my privacy and confidentiality be protected?
Field Label: Your privacy is important to us. Identifiable information will be stored securely at the University of Tasmania and accessed only by authorised members of the research team. Study data will be analysed and reported in a way that does not identify you.

Section Header: 9. Do I have to take part and can I withdraw?
Field Label: Taking part in this study is voluntary. You may choose not to take part, or to withdraw at any time, without giving a reason. Your decision will not affect your current or future health care.

Section Header: 10. What will happen to the data when this study is over?
Field Label: When the study is finished, all information will be stored on a password protected University of Tasmania server that only the research team can access. All information for the study will be destroyed after 15 years in accordance with University of Tasmania Human Research Ethics Committee recommendations for clinical trials and Good Clinical Practice Guidelines. Study data will be kept in a de-identified database for future research, including disclosure to other approved researchers outside this study.

Section Header: 11. Will I have access to the intervention after the study ends?
Field Label: The intervention used in this study - AOBP - may continue to be available at this clinic after the study ends. Ongoing access is not guaranteed and depends on whether the clinic adopts AOBP in usual practice, with any continued use determined by your general practitioner.

Section Header: 12. How is the study being funded?
Field Label: This study is funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC), with support from partner organisations involved in primary health care and cardiovascular health.

Seated AOBP Instructions
Read the following instructions word-for-word to the patient:
  • I am now going to ask you to sit quietly and relax while we measure your blood pressure.
  • There must be no distractions the whole time.
  • Please turn your phone off and avoid talking during the whole time.
  • It is also important to stay in the seated position because changes can influence the AOBP readings.
  • Once I start the device, I will leave the room.
  • The device will automatically count down a 5-minute rest period and then begin recording 3 BP readings at 30-second intervals.
  • The device will automatically record a (fourth) measurement to see if you have a normal heart rhythm.
  • This process should take about 8 minutes.
  • I will return once the measures are done.
